header:
Date: 2025-06-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Rafi Chen (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Vela, Platform Eng), Arjun Mehta (Vela, Sec Arch), Priya Rao (Vela, PM)
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked Vela through multi-tenant rate limiting, org/project key model, per-route quotas, key scoping and rotation. Discussed console UI for setting soft/hard quotas, burst policies, and Optimize suggestions for lowering unit cost. Vela interested in piloting with two projects; agreed actions around sending pricing, sample configs, and scheduling a benchmark pilot.
transcript: 00:00 Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — quick roll call?
00:05 Lina (Vela): Hi, Lina here, platform eng — we have Arjun and Priya on as well.
00:12 Rafi (SE): Rafi from Redwood — I'll drive the console demo after Maya covers the org-level flow.
00:20 Maya: Cool, goal for today is to show how org keys and project keys let you isolate tenants, set quotas and throttles, and how Optimize suggests batch/quant settings. We'll leave time for Q&A.
01:03 Arjun: Quick context — we manage a multi-tenant ingestion service, want per-customer rate limits, but also fine-grained per-route caps. Security is big: key rotation and audit logs required.
01:40 Maya: Perfect, that maps to what we typically show. Any hard requirements on residency or KMS?
01:50 Arjun: No residency for pilot; we do need customer-managed keys for production — KMS integration is a check box for us.
02:15 Rafi: Noted. On Redwood Private we support KMS/HSM integrations and exportable audit logs; we'll include the compliance excerpt. Alright, going into the Console now — sharing my screen.

03:05 Rafi: Top-left is the org view. You can create org keys that span projects, a project key scoped to a single project, and ephemeral keys for short-lived jobs. Example: Vela-org-2025 — you can set default quota profiles at the org level.
03:48 Lina: How do org keys affect billing? If we have one org key, how are costs attributed to projects?
04:05 Maya: Good question — billing is tied to project IDs. Org keys authorize across projects but usage gets tagged by project. You can also enforce project-level quotas to keep spend isolated.
04:30 Priya: Can we force-inject a project tag if a client uses the org key incorrectly?

04:42 Rafi: Yes, there is server-side enforcement: if you don't supply a project header, we can auto-assign a default project mapping or reject the request. That mapping can be overridden by a route policy.
05:10 Rafi: I'm clicking into Policies -> Rate Limits. There are prebuilt templates: per-second TPS, per-minute token limits, and burst windows. You can attach them to projects or API routes.
05:45 Lina: We need burst handling for synchronous inference spikes; typical burst is 500 rps for short windows.
06:00 Rafi: In the UI we set a soft limit (throttled response with Retry-After header) and a hard limit (reject with 429). Also a leaky-bucket for smoothing.
06:35 Arjun: How deterministic is the Retry-After? We have clients that auto-backoff; need accurate headers.
06:47 Rafi: Retry-After is set based on the bucket fullness estimate; it's best-effort but respects SLOs. We can also emit a webhook to your operations when throttling kicks in.

07:15 Maya: Now API view — example curl: POST /v1/generate with header X-Redwood-Project: vela-search. If you pass org-key instead, the project header is used to attribute but rate limits are applied in order: route -> project -> org.
07:55 Lina: So evaluation order matters — route level first?
08:05 Rafi: Correct. Route policies are most specific. If route is within project quota and project quota is within org quota, it passes. If any fails, the request is throttled or rejected.
08:40 Priya: Can we set separate token quotas vs request quotas? We have heavy embeddings that are tokens-heavy but low request count.
08:55 Rafi: Yes, quotas can be token-based (per-token) or request-based. You can combine them; e.g., 10k tokens/day and 5k requests/day.
09:20 Lina: How do we handle shared pools — if one project spikes, can others borrow capacity?

09:33 Rafi: Two patterns: conservative (strict isolation) or shared-burst. Shared-burst allows projects to borrow unused headroom from the org pool until org hard cap is reached. You configure policies in the org quota profile.
10:05 Arjun: Any precedence for Dedicated vs Hosted? For pilot AWS-hosted is fine, but we may want Dedicated later.
10:20 Maya: Dedicated has guaranteed reserved capacity and you can opt for stricter isolation. The rate-limit semantics are the same; Dedicated simply has predictable throughput and SLOs.

11:00 Rafi: Switching to key management — in Keys tab you can create keys, set TTLs, rotate, and restrict scopes: allowed projects, allowed models, allowed routes. Here's creating a project-scoped key: name, TTL 30d, scopes: embeddings:create only.
11:45 Priya: TTLs — can we auto-rotate monthly and have automatic revocation if compromised?
11:55 Rafi: Yes, automated rotation with overlap windows is supported. You can schedule rotation and set a policy to revoke older keys immediately upon rotation or keep 24h overlap.
12:30 Lina: We also want audit trails. How fine-grained are audit logs?
12:38 Rafi: Audit logs include key usage, route, project, token counts, and caller IP. They can be pushed to your SIEM or downloaded. We'll include the log schema in the follow-up.

13:05 Maya: Quick aside — Optimize will look at request patterns and suggest batching rules, cache prefixes, and quantization profiles to lower spend while preserving latency. We'll demo a recommendation later.
13:32 Rafi: Now a short demo of a per-route quota: attaching a quota to /v1/embeddings that is token-based with burst window 60s, soft limit 20k tokens/60s, hard 25k tokens/60s. Simulating traffic...
14:10 (sound of keyboard)
14:15 Rafi: Ok simulation shows throttling hits at 14:18, console shows a spike chart and a list of affected keys — you can click a key to see recent requests and token counts.
15:00 Lina: Will the simulation reflect live KV-cache hits? We have prefix caching for repeated prompts.
15:12 Rafi: The simulator is synthetic; live cache hit-rate is measured by the runtime and reported. We do have a metric for KV cache hit-rate and prefix hits in the console.
15:40 Priya: On the API side, is there an SDK that surfaces Retry-After automatic backoff?
15:50 Maya: Our SDKs include an exponential backoff with jitter and respect 429 Retry-After when present. We can share SDK snippets for node/python.
16:20 Arjun: Security question — if an attacker exfiltrates an org key, can we scope and quarantine it without rotating all keys?
16:33 Rafi: You can create a quarantine policy: mark a key as revoked, reassign traffic to a new key, and optionally blacklist IP ranges. If keys are project-scoped you limit blast radius.
17:05 Lina: Are there rate-limit headers in responses so our gateway can expose them upstream?
17:15 Rafi: Yes: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, and Retry-After when throttled. Note that token-based limits map to token headers as well.
17:55 Priya: Let's talk SSO and RBAC — can we enforce who creates org keys?
18:05 Maya: Yes, admin roles at the org level, and granular RBAC for key creation. We integrate with SAML/SCIM so users sync from your IdP.
18:45 Arjun: Does the audit log record role changes and key creation events?
18:52 Rafi: It does — create, rotate, revoke events are recorded with actor and timestamp.
19:20 Lina: For billing, can we enforce hard spend caps per project to prevent runaway costs?
19:33 Rafi: There is a spend cap feature that can block further requests when a project hits a spend threshold. You can also send alerts when hitting percent thresholds.

20:10 Maya: Now switching to Optimize recommendations — here's a sample report based on your traffic (synthetic demo): recommends batching 8 requests for embeddings, enable prefix cache for repeated prompts, consider int8 quantization on non-critical models to save 30% cost.
20:50 Priya: How do we validate quality after quantization?
21:00 Rafi: Optimize ties into evals — you can run a prompt set before and after quantization and it will show regressions. We can gate rollouts on no-regression criteria.
21:35 Lina: For pilot, we'd like to test two projects: search and recommendations. Search is low-latency, recs can accept higher latency. How do we express latency SLOs?
21:50 Rafi: In rollout policies you can set latency SLOs per route; if quantization or model change increases p95 beyond threshold, automatic rollback occurs.
22:25 Maya: Quick live API example — sending a high-volume loop with org-key vs project-key and showing difference in attribution and throttles. Starting loop...
23:10 (simulator noise)
23:18 Rafi: Loop shows requests from org-key with mixed project headers, the console attributes to projects and the project that exceeded got a 429s while other projects continued.
24:05 Arjun: Any limits on number of keys or projects? We manage hundreds of internal projects.
24:18 Rafi: No hard limit on projects; UI supports pagination and bulk import. Keys count is practical limits; we recommend naming conventions and tag-based grouping.
24:55 Priya: Can we enforce per-customer SLA tiers (gold/silver) with different rate-limits?
25:05 Rafi: Absolutely — policy templates can be applied by tag. Gold gets higher default burst and lower preemption; silver is more constrained.
25:40 Lina: Monitoring — can we get per-key telemetry into Datadog?
25:50 Rafi: Yes, metrics export to Datadog/Prometheus/Kinesis via our metrics sink. We can push per-key, per-route metrics and throttling events.
26:20 Maya: Quick note on pricing: org-level pricing is usage-based; Dedicated/reserved capacity has committed spend but lower unit price. I'll send a pricing matrix.
26:45 Priya: For the pilot we're leaning hosted initially, but want to evaluate Dedicated if predictability is better priced.
27:00 Rafi: For benchmarks we'll include both hosted and an emulated reserved profile so you can compare latency/throughput and unit-cost.
27:35 Maya: Let's demo the webhook alerting when a project reaches 80% quota — creating an alert now, targeting the recs project, threshold 80% of daily token quota.
28:05 (click)
28:12 Rafi: There — event will POST to your webhook. You can set escalation and slack integration too.
28:45 Arjun: Need to confirm if webhook payload includes request examples and anonymized tokens for forensic purposes.
28:58 Rafi: Payload includes key id, route, project id, timestamp, and aggregated token counts. For security we omit raw prompts unless you opt-in for debug mode behind secure channel.
29:30 Priya: What about request replay for debugging?
29:38 Rafi: We have an opt-in request replay buffer for 24-72h with PII scrubbers; needs explicit consent and controls.
30:05 Maya: Time check — ~16 minutes left. Any big remaining items?
30:15 Lina: I'd like to see the sample rate-limit config JSON and a short curl to create a project-scoped key.
30:30 Rafi: I'll paste sample in chat — curl POST /v1/keys {name, scopes:[project:vela-search], ttl:30d} and sample rate-limit JSON with token and request caps.
31:05 (chat paste)
31:10 Priya: Also want to confirm key rotation SLA — if we rotate keys automatically, what's the downtime window?
31:22 Rafi: Typically zero-downtime if you allow overlap; if you force immediate revoke, calls using old key will fail until clients update. We recommend overlap of 24h for safe rollout.
31:50 Arjun: For the pilot, we'll need sample SG configs for IP allowlist and VPC egress rules.
32:00 Maya: Noted — we'll include network egress doc and examples for AWS security groups and private connectivity patterns.
32:35 Rafi: Back to Optimize: we can run a dry-run that simulates cost savings and shows expected latency change. That helps you validate quantization tradeoffs.
33:05 Lina: How easy to rollback a quantized model in production?
33:12 Rafi: Rollouts are per-route; you can do canaries and automatic rollback if evals fail. It's in the Console under Model Rollouts.
33:40 Priya: Any gotchas about KV cache and multi-tenant isolation? We don't want cross-tenant cache poisoning.
33:52 Rafi: KV cache is namespaced by project id and model variant by default, so isolation is enforced. You can also enable stricter per-key namespaces.
34:30 Maya: Quick recap of what we'll send: pricing matrix, SOC2 excerpt, sample rate-limit JSON, API key scoping doc, network egress examples, and a proposed pilot plan.
35:05 Arjun: Sounds good. On pilot plan — can we get a 2-week pilot with 2 projects and an initial traffic replay?
35:15 Maya: Yes — we'll scope that and include steps for replay, metrics to capture, and success criteria.
35:40 Lina: Success metrics: 99th p95 latency for search < 120ms, embedding cost per 1k tokens reduced by > 20% if using Optimize suggestions, zero security incidents.
36:05 Rafi: We'll add those to the pilot playbook. Also will include a sample eval set for quality gating.
36:40 Priya: One more question — can we enforce per-user quotas inside a project?
36:50 Rafi: Yes, you can use subkeys or tag requests with user-id and apply rate-limits based on those tags for fine-grained controls.
37:25 Maya: We're at ~9 minutes left — open Q&A?
37:33 Arjun: Do you have a reference architecture for hybrid: hosted control plane, private data plane?
37:45 Rafi: Yes, we call it 'split-control' — control plane managed by Redwood, data plane in your VPC; keys and telemetry flow over secure channels. We'll attach the reference diagram.
38:20 Lina: Any concerns about latency from private data plane for EU region?
38:30 Rafi: Latency depends on proximity to GPUs; we have EU edge zones. For VPC we recommend colocating compute in same region as your services.
38:58 Priya: Ok final: who will set up the pilot agreement?
39:05 Maya: I'll coordinate with growth and your procurement. For now, I'll send a pilot SOW draft and pricing options.
39:30 (brief pause)
39:40 Rafi: Wrapping up — last demo note: policy evaluation order, token vs request caps, shared-burst option, webhook alerts, and Optimize integration for batching/quantization.
40:10 Priya: Thanks, that was super helpful.
40:20 Lina: Thanks, Maya and Rafi. We'll review and respond with pilot timeline.
40:28 Maya: Great — we'll email the docs and schedule the benchmark. Any final items?
41:00 Arjun: One ask — include a sample webhook payload for throttling events with anonymized example.
41:12 Rafi: Will do. Also including example Datadog metric names.
41:40 Maya: Ok closing notes: next call — pilot kickoff; proposed 2025-06-24 16:00 UTC. Does that work?
41:55 Priya: Works for us.
42:05 Lina: Works.
42:12 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up. Bye.
45:30 (meeting ended)
